Sully’s Misfits Kitchen, Fuquay Varina: A Taste of Boston for the NC Triangle

You are here: Home / Restaurant & Bar Reviews / Fuquay-Varina / Sully’s Misfits Kitchen, Fuquay Varina: A Taste of Boston for the NC Triangle
November 17, 2026 by Ron Wen
Spread the love
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:48
Instaread

While I’ve been in North Carolina for 20 years, I must confess about my origins: I’m a Yankee and Northerner by birth! While I have spent time in the San Francisco area, I actually grew up mostly in the Boston area for over 20 years. And as an ex-New Englander, I admit to having cravings from time to time. For regional favorites like lobster rolls, clam chowder, and pupu platters. So I have to admit to being intrigued when I heard about Sully’s Misfits Kitchen down in Fuquay-Varina! Marketed as a taste of the South Shore, Massachusetts, which is oddly specific. A quick scan of the menu and I’m ready to go visit. Here’s what to expect if you head on down to the Quay and visit to Sully’s Misfits Kitchen…

Sully’s Misfits Kitchen, Fuquay-Varina – Location, Interior

If you want to dine at Sully’s, head on over to the Brick, about 30 minutes south of Raleigh! It’s an interesting, wedge-shaped building that is a deep-red brick color. Maybe an old-school, mill-type industrial building. Inside, you’ll find a casual dive-sports bar populated with locals hanging out. Head to the back where you’ll find some dart boards and a more open dining area populated with 4-tops. You can order online at Sully’s website or hop on over to the white order kiosk in back.

Sully’s Misfits Kitchen, Fuquay-Varina – Menu, Food

Now here’s where things get interesting! Scanning the menu, I notice a couple of unique items. Beef and chicken teriyaki skewers? Check, a traditional item in Chinese restaurants in the Boston area. Portuguese fries? Well, the Boston area has a substantial Portuguese population on the North Shore, so I’m not terribly surprised. And the North Shore roast beef?! Oh yes, that is traditional Boston food, typically delivered by a local restaurant favorite: Kelly’s Roast Beef. The menu at Sully’s Misfit Kitchen is the real, Massachusetts, deal.

Since this is my first visit, we order up a large assortment of items at the kiosk, grab a beer and hang out at a 4-top. The food takes a bit of time; they’ve got a lot of ToGo orders, and I see the staff hustling out order after order. But we start receiving our food, served up in black plastic containers. First up are the VERY tasty steak tip egg rolls which are on special. The outside wrapper is bubbly and crunchy while the inside is full of steaky goodness and cheese. I’m pretty certain the steak used are likely the same as their teriyaki beef skewers.

Next on our ToEat list are the classic Buffalo wings! With 10 to an order, it’s a messy but delicious bite of chicken. A solid wing, if not outstanding. Sully’s does $1 wing night on Monday if you’re a fan and want to save some money.

Moving on to the mains, I ordered up the 3-way North Shore roast beef! Wrapped in aluminum foil, this was a terribly messy eat for me. But I mean in a totally great way! The sandwich features warm, thin-sliced roast beef on an onion roll with American cheese, mayo, and a sloppy dousing of James River barbeque sauce! It’s an incredibly unique combination of beef, rich fattiness with the tangy barbeque sauce counter-balancing it all. A must-do even if you’re not familiar with this type of sandwich!

And finally, the bar pizza! It’s a bit different than what I’ve tried before: Midwestern bar-type pizzas. Our pepperoni pie was baked in a pan, showing off a browned, lacy cheese edge and well-topped with cheese and sauce. It’s a small pie but full of flavor and richness, a very tasty slice.

Sully’s Misfits Kitchen, Fuquay-Varina – Service, Conclusion

Since you order online and the food is brought to you, service is a pretty simple scenario. But you can certainly tell that the owner is passionate about the menu and food. I saw him hustling dishes out from time to time, and they do make sure you get your eats in a timely fashion. While I’m pretty sure they will clear your table, we self-bussed whatever we could to keep the dining room clean.

As an ex-New Englander, I have to say that I really enjoyed dining at Sully’s Misfits Kitchen. While the name is a mouthful, so is the delicious food on the menu! It definitely brought back some memories for me after living in the Bah-stan area. But I think even local NC people will really enjoy what they’re serving up. So give Sully’s a try if you’re in the Fuquay-Varina area. And if you’re ordering up that 3-way roast beef sandwich, make sure you grab some extra napkins off of the orange toolbox. I’m pretty sure you’ll be needing them, bon appetit!

Sully’s Misfits Kitchen in The Brick
213 Fayetteville St, Fuquay-Varina, NC 27526
919.980.2773
